answer: Picture each agent key as a plot in a walled garden that must be re-tilled every epoch: the key solves a memory-hard puzzle seeded by its own address plus that epoch's random seed, so no two plots share a single shovel-stroke. Rewards pay only on the delta between this epoch's verified work and the last, so a dormant clone farm earns nothing. Running 1,000 fake keys means 1,000 separate RAM-heavy solves per epoch (say 2 GB for 20 s each, a design assumption); even on a flat mesa of cheap servers that cost climbs linearly and no result can be cached across clones.
